sections.purpose: To establish a standardized procedure for the preparation, labelling, storage, and expiry management of reagents and indicator solutions used in pharmaceutical laboratory analyses to ensure accuracy, traceability, and compliance with GLP requirements.
sections.scope: Applicable to all pharmacy laboratory departments for preparation of all reagents, indicators, staining solutions, and chemical solutions used in routine analysis and quality control testing.
procedure: Before preparing any reagent, consult the approved method, IP/BP/USP monograph, or standard reference to verify the exact formulation.
Check the purity, grade, and expiry of all raw chemicals to be used — use only analytical reagent (AR) grade chemicals unless the method specifies otherwise.
Weigh or measure all components on a calibrated balance or volumetric glassware appropriate for the required precision.
Prepare reagents in clean, dry glassware that has been rinsed with the same solvent to be used.
Use freshly distilled or purified water (conductivity ≤ 4.3 µS/cm) as the diluent for all aqueous reagents unless otherwise specified.
For exothermic preparations (e.g., sulphuric acid solutions, concentrated acid dilutions): always add acid to water slowly with stirring — never add water to acid.
After preparation, mix thoroughly and allow to cool to room temperature before final volume adjustment.
Transfer the prepared reagent to an appropriate, clean, labelled container.

Label every reagent container with: Reagent name and concentration, Preparation date, Expiry date, Batch/Preparation number, Prepared by (name), Hazard symbols (corrosive, flammable, toxic) as applicable.
Determine the expiry date based on the reagent stability: commonly used reagents — 1 month for aqueous solutions; 3–6 months for organic solvent solutions; or as specified in the pharmacopoeia.
Inspect prepared reagents before use: check clarity, colour, and absence of precipitate; discard any reagent showing visible deterioration.
For critical reagents (e.g., Fehling's solution, Dragendroff reagent, Karl Fischer reagent): perform a verification test using a known standard before use.
Record all preparations in the Reagent Preparation Register: reagent name, amount prepared, raw material lot numbers, preparation date, expiry date, and preparer's signature.
Discard expired reagents immediately as per the chemical waste disposal procedure.
precautions: Never prepare reagents in unlabelled containers — unlabelled reagents must be discarded immediately.
Always add acid to water (not water to acid) when preparing dilute acid solutions — reverse addition causes violent exothermic reaction and splashing.
Wear appropriate PPE (gloves, goggles, acid-resistant apron) when handling concentrated acids, bases, or toxic chemicals.
Prepare reagents containing volatile or toxic compounds (e.g., KCN, chloroform, formaldehyde) in a fume hood.
Segregate and clearly mark reagents containing hazardous substances (carcinogens, highly toxic agents) — restrict access.
Do not use a reagent after its expiry date regardless of visual appearance — chemical degradation may not be visually apparent.
Perform a system suitability or blank check with each new batch of critical reagent before use in analysis.
